modernizationFindings.title: EXEC SQL without SQLCODE / SQLSTATE check
modernizationFindings.description: Embedded SQL with no SQLCODE / SQLSTATE inspection after the call and no WHENEVER directive in effect. Unhandled SQL errors are a common source of silent data corruption in COBOL.
modernizationFindings.suggestedReplacement:
EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC.
    IF SQLCODE NOT = ZERO
        PERFORM HANDLE-SQL-ERROR
    END-IF.

modernizationFindings.description: PERFORM-UNTIL containing a READ is the classic COBOL "read each record" loop. When backed by a database, replace with a single SELECT and result-set iteration; when backed by a file, consider streaming with explicit termination handling.
modernizationFindings.suggestedReplacement:
EXEC SQL DECLARE CUR CURSOR FOR
    SELECT * FROM <table> WHERE ... END-EXEC.
EXEC SQL OPEN CUR END-EXEC.
PERFORM UNTIL SQLCODE = 100
    EXEC SQL FETCH CUR INTO :record END-EXEC
END-PERFORM.
